newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares find support in fall, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares find support in fall, seen stable.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged down early on Monday on speculative selling by Russian operators after recent strong gains, but traders forecast prices would not fall any further as shares found support.
UES power utility ordinaries fell to $0.4115 at 0925 GMT from Friday's closing $0.4165, Rostelekom was down to $4.41 from $4.50 and LUKoil fell to $20.50 from $21.15.

"Traders decided to speculate on a fall, but all shares met support," Alfa-Capital Deputy Sales Director Alexei Genkin said. "Now leading prices are lower than Friday's close, but they are firm. I do not think a lot will happen today, everything will remain at current levels."
Traders forecast lively trading in second-tier oil shares, which had lagged behind other stocks in last month's rise.

"After a sharp rise in the last two days of such paper as Yuganskneftegaz and Purneftegaz we should expect a rise in a similar group of shares, which are few and only see five or 10 deals a week," a Western trader said.
He said Chernogorneft and Kondpetroleum had a growth potential.

"I am not saying there will certainly be growth in Kondpetroleum," the trader said. "But if somebody looks into its fundamentals and would like to buy for $1-$1.5 million there will be a rise of 30-40 percent."
Yuganskneftegaz was priced at $29.10, Purneftegaz $6.15 Chernogorneft $11.30 and Kondpetroleum $2.20 on July 18, when they were last traded.
The trader said there was interest in other oil companies, which are not traded on the Russian Trading System's first tier, such as Transneft oil pipe company.
